translations.answer: The thread confirms that the seed is set after environment construction, and terrain generation, PhysX initialization, and internal buffer initialization may have already consumed random numbers. PR #940 moves the cfg seed to the front of the environment constructor and tests for consistent observation and reward; the original author also reported that the repeated training curve aligns after moving the seed forward. The fix only closes the initialization order issue and does not guarantee full determination of rough terrain, cross-hardware, or entire PPO training chain.
translations.applicability: Applicable to Isaac Lab pipelines lacking PR #940, or where the seed is still later than environment construction. Exact determinism boundaries must be verified in the same hardware and fixed version.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict, and it has been formally documented or independently reproducible with exact references.
translations.details.attempts.0: The original author moved the seed from after environment construction to before.
translations.details.attempts.1: PR #940 sets the seed as the first operation of the environment constructor and adds observation/reward consistency testing.
translations.details.attempts.2: Subsequent users use env.reset(seed=YOUR_SEED), constant actions, or seeded random actions to drive the environment.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Setting the cfg seed before environment construction avoids terrain, PhysX, or internal buffer initialization from consuming random numbers.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: After calling env.reset(seed=YOUR_SEED), use constant actions or seeded random actions to drive the environment.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Aggregate and hash environment tensors such as observation and reward, and compare them across the same hardware and continuous runs; only then check PPO action sampling.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use the version containing PR #940, or ensure the environment seed is active before environment, terrain, and simulation object construction.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: In specific later cases, use env.reset(seed=...) to fix the issue of seed not taking effect when Hydra args.seed=None.
translations.details.environments.0: Original post: Isaac Sim 2024.4.1, Ubuntu 22.04, RTX 3090, CUDA 11.2, driver 550; no exact IsaacLab commit provided.
translations.details.environments.1: Maintainer PR #940 is performed in the same process with fixed step observation/reward consistency testing and three runs with ANYmal rough locomotion.
translations.details.environments.2: Subsequent users only specify the same hardware and continuous simulation for up to 2000 steps, but no full version matrix provided.
translations.details.limits.0: PR testing only confirms same process/specific task and version, and does not guarantee cross-hardware, cross-Isaac Sim version, or GPU scheduling consistency.
translations.details.limits.1: The three training graphs from the maintainer are not used in this card's conclusion; only the text explanation and PR testing code are used.
translations.details.limits.2: The difference in rough terrain has not been closed by the maintainer, so it cannot be claimed that setting the seed ensures all training curves align.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author reported that multiple reward curves aligned after moving the seed forward; the maintainer tested in the same process and got the same observation/reward.
translations.details.outcomes.1: Subsequent users reported consistent environment tensors after 2000 steps on the same hardware, but their PPO action sampling remains uncertain.
translations.details.outcomes.2: The rough terrain difference is still not closed by other users.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When the training curve is still inconsistent after setting the seed, when does the seed become effective?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How can we separate the environment simulation's non-determinism from the PPO action generation's non-determinism?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Reproducibility conclusions should be bound to hardware, driver, Isaac Sim/IsaacLab commit, and task config; control algorithm comparisons should report multiple seed distributions.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The maintainer believes that terrain generation, PhysX solver, and internal buffer initialization in the initial phase of the initialization process were random in the old process.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The 2000-step isolation test by subsequent users locates the remaining difference in their specific environment to PPO action generation.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Training reward curves do not align for the same seed.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Even with a fixed terrain seed, some users report slight differences in the first few iterations of observation/reward and these differences gradually increase.
translations.source.locator: IsaacLab #904 original post resolution; maintainer explanation 2320250794, test 2333392825; PR #940
translations.source.title: Isaac Lab reproducibility should distinguish between environment initialization randomness and strategy algorithm randomness
translations.title: Isaac Lab: Training curves still inconsistent after setting seed, why set seed before environment construction?
